title: PINN-FEM Framework for Hyperelastic Biomechanics Simulation
subtitle: Master's Thesis - Physics-Informed Neural Networks - Computational Biomechanics
description: Development of a Physics-Informed Neural Network framework to approximate FEM displacement fields in 3D hyperelastic materials, combining Mooney-Rivlin modeling, boundary condition enforcement and neural network optimization.
highlights: Implemented a FEM reference workflow for a 3D hyperelastic solid under mixed Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions.
Developed a PINN-based approximation of the displacement field using physics-informed loss terms.
Modeled large-deformation hyperelastic behavior through a Mooney-Rivlin strain energy formulation.
Studied the effect of architecture, activation functions, optimizers and loss-weighting strategies on training performance.
Analyzed the role of the Dirichlet penalty weight in accurately reproducing FEM displacement fields.
Extended the framework toward inverse material parameter identification.

title: Gen Z Burnout Risk Classification with Neural Networks
subtitle: Multiclass neural network classification on tabular behavioral data
image: public/images/projects/Gen Z Burnout Risk Classification with Neural Networks.png
description: Deep learning project focused on multiclass classification of burnout risk in Gen Z using tabular lifestyle, mental wellness and digital behavior variables.
highlights: Built a supervised multiclass classification pipeline for Burnout_Risk with Low, Medium and High classes.
Applied stratified train-validation-test splitting, z-score scaling, one-hot encoding and class weighting.
Compared a linear baseline, shallow neural network, Keras Tuner search and deeper MLP architectures.
Studied the effect of activation functions, dropout intensity and optimizers on model performance.
Selected a deep MLP with dropout, ReLU activation and RMSprop as the best-performing configuration.
Interpreted results with accuracy, class-wise precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix and training curves.

title: Production Scheduling Optimization on Unrelated Parallel Machines
subtitle: Operations Research & Scheduling Optimization
image: public/images/projects/Production Scheduling Optimization on Unrelated Parallel Machines.png
description: Operations research project focused on production scheduling in unrelated parallel machines, comparing exact and metaheuristic approaches under progressively more realistic constraints.
highlights: Modeled an unrelated parallel machine scheduling problem with 50 jobs and 5 machines.
Implemented a base exact model in Excel/OpenSolver and used it as a benchmark.
Developed Python-based solution approaches using CP-SAT, a Genetic Algorithm and Iterated Greedy.
Extended the base problem with release dates, sequence-dependent setups, precedence relations and resource constraints.
Compared methods across increasing levels of complexity using Relative Percentage Deviation.
Generated reproducible synthetic extensions using fixed random seeds and structured input files.

title: Gen Z Mental Wellness Multivariate Monitoring
subtitle: PCA, PLS, PLS-DA and process monitoring applied to psychological wellbeing data
description: Multivariate analysis project focused on Gen Z mental wellness, combining PCA, PLS, PCR, PLS-DA, Hotelling's T2, SPE diagnostics and Random Forest classification to study lifestyle habits, anxiety and burnout risk.
highlights: Explored latent structures in lifestyle, digital habits and psychological wellbeing variables using PCA.
Compared MLR, PCR and PLS models for explaining Anxiety_Score from lifestyle and digital exposure variables.
Applied Hotelling's T2 and SPE diagnostics to identify extreme or poorly represented observations without applying mechanical deletion rules.
Built and interpreted a PLS-DA model for burnout risk discrimination and compared it with a Random Forest classifier.
image: public/images/projects/Gen Z Mental Wellness Multivariate Monitoring.png

title: Time Series Forecasting of Wind Energy Generation in Spain
subtitle: ARIMA-based forecasting and temporal analysis in R
image: public/images/projects/Time Series Forecasting of Wind Energy Generation in Spain.png
description: Industrial time series forecasting project focused on modelling and predicting wind energy generation in Spain using ARIMA-based methods in R.
highlights: Developed a time series forecasting project in R using Spanish wind power generation data.
Applied temporal preprocessing, exploratory analysis and ARIMA-based forecasting methodology.
Evaluated the behaviour of wind energy generation over time and interpreted the forecasting performance.
Built a reproducible analytical workflow combining industrial data, statistical modeling and visualization.

title: Healthcare Cost Analytics with Multivariate Methods
subtitle: Healthcare Analytics with PCA, MCA, clustering and supervised modeling
image: public/images/projects/Healthcare Cost Analytics with Multivariate Methods.png
description: Multivariate analysis project focused on understanding and modeling annual medical insurance costs using dimensionality reduction, categorical data analysis, clustering and supervised classification techniques.
highlights: Analyzed a healthcare insurance dataset with demographic, clinical, lifestyle, policy and cost-related variables.
Applied PCA to synthesize economic, contractual and clinical information into interpretable latent dimensions.
Combined PCA with regression modeling to study annual medical cost while reducing multicollinearity.
Used MCA to explore associations between categorical health, lifestyle and personal profile variables.
Applied clustering on MCA coordinates to identify homogeneous behavioral and insurance-related profiles.
Built LDA models to classify insured individuals into low, medium and high annual cost groups.

title: Student Sleep and Wellbeing Statistical Analysis in R
subtitle: Applied statistics, hypothesis testing and regression modeling in R
image: public/images/projects/Student Sleep and Wellbeing Statistical Analysis in R.png
description: R-based statistical analysis project studying the relationship between sleep habits, emotional wellbeing and academic performance in university students, including data cleaning, imputation, hypothesis testing and regression modeling.
highlights: Performed exploratory analysis and variable type definition for a university student sleep and wellbeing dataset.
Detected constant and near-constant variables, anomalous values, outliers and missing data patterns.
Applied multiple imputation using mice and assessed normality using Shapiro-Wilk tests.
Used Box-Cox transformations, Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression.
Applied Kruskal-Wallis, ANOVA, Levene and Wilcoxon / Mann-Whitney tests.
Summarized relationships between sleep habits, chronotype, wellbeing indicators and academic performance through visual reporting.

title: Effective Mechanical Power in Pediatric Mechanical Ventilation
subtitle: Bachelor's Thesis awarded with Honors - Biomedical Data Analysis
description: Biomedical data analysis project focused on estimating Effective Mechanical Power as a potential indicator of ventilatory aggressiveness in mechanically ventilated pediatric patients.
highlights: Analyzed clinical and ventilatory data from pediatric mechanical ventilation cases.
Developed MATLAB-based analytical workflows to estimate mechanical power-related metrics.
Studied Effective Mechanical Power as a candidate indicator of ventilatory aggressiveness.
Built reproducible scripts for preprocessing, calculation and visualization of derived variables.
Connected biomedical engineering, clinical interpretation and quantitative analysis.
Bachelor's Thesis awarded with Honors.

title: DermaMNIST Skin Lesion Classification
subtitle: Deep learning comparison for multiclass skin lesion classification
description: Academic comparison of a custom CNN, ImageNet transfer learning, radiology-domain transfer learning and dermatology-oriented pretraining for multiclass skin lesion classification on DermaMNIST.
highlights: Compared six deep learning configurations for multiclass skin lesion classification using DermaMNIST.
Evaluated a custom CNN, ImageNet transfer learning, RadImageNet/RAC initialization and a dermatology-oriented MaxNet/ISIC reference.
Prioritized Macro F1, Balanced Accuracy, Macro Recall and Cohen's Kappa to account for class imbalance.
Used bootstrap-based uncertainty estimates and aggregate visual comparisons to support model interpretation.
Kept raw datasets, clinical images, checkpoints and external pretrained weights out of the public repository.
